canonical_documentation_delta_proposed.text: Record PR306's original Windows failure against synthetic checkout 522b7bc6e7e9207dac0c745b49d90907ecdf3080 (tree a31db4434c7bbe69bf572626d2174f64f9ff2f39; ordered parents 6181b044c75de35386f1ae30e71725398b6a7feb and fada8e068f61f6e0e380ec4685eed2f4cf0b9ade). Its five integration failures timed out in the first 90-second ready-port wait before the catalog/history/generation assertions. One instrumented failure had no ready marker at 80/88 seconds and, after the separate 20-second cleanup, one live descendant with execution_stopped=false and descendant_reap_complete=false. A separate caller reported holotree variables at 87.2 seconds. These observations do not establish the readiness cause or connect the child to it; retain startup and cleanup as separate unresolved gates, and qualify the refreshed e2-based head independently.

One instrumented failure snapshot shows wrapper reaped, zero host readers active, one observed live descendant, execution_stopped=false, descendant_reap_complete=false. This does not establish that the child caused the readiness timeout.

finding: No specific root cause is proven. The run proves first-readiness timeouts on a 6181+fada synthetic checkout, plus a separate incomplete child cleanup observation. It does not prove a defect in the SQLite savepoint change, a general Windows infrastructure cause, or that the survivor caused the startup timeout.
